# migration_name: # phase must be expand, contract, or metadata-only.
# previous_expand_release is required for destructive contract migrations; use n/a otherwise.
# old_code_compatible must be exactly one of yes, no, or windowed; any other value fails the gate.

#   yes = genuinely old-code compatible, because the migration carries a compensating pattern (e.g. SET NOT NULL paired with a same-column non-NULL SET DEFAULT, so an old colour's omitted-column INSERT still succeeds).

#   windowed = NOT compatible: the previous colour will error between migrate and cutover. Needs a maintenance window plus the ALLOW_BREAKING_BLUE_GREEN_MIGRATIONS override, and the incompatibility and window plan must be written into lock_impact_plan. Do not assert yes for one of these - windowed is what the value exists for.
#   no = a migration with no breaking SQL matched by the deploy guard; nothing to acknowledge.
# A migration with breaking SQL matched by the deploy guard must be yes or windowed. See docs/BLUE_GREEN_MIGRATION_POLICY.md for the rollback boundary a windowed migration moves.

# #2596 rollback ordering for 20260806010000 is part of its lock-impact plan: KEEP the new runtime and cron/drain available while the club row and EVERY explicit lodge ENFORCED override are demoted; after the last override change, require zero unprocessed HostingCoverageReevaluation rows (max-attempt/lastError rows are blockers) and zero unresolved HostingCoverageIncident rows; repeat all three proofs, and only then stop every new worker and start the old-only release. Its rollback.sql carries the exact queries. The nullable columns and applied migration history remain intact.

lock_impact_plan: Hosting-coverage queue and owner-notification claimant fencing (#2596). THE SQL IS ADDITIVE BUT THE MIXED-RUNTIME PROTOCOL IS NOT COMPATIBLE. One nullable VARCHAR(64) opaque claim-token column is added to HostingCoverageIncident, and nullable VARCHAR(64) claim-token plus nullable TIMESTAMP(3) claim-expiry columns are added to HostingCoverageReevaluation. Both are low-volume compliance tables introduced by 20260803070000; PostgreSQL adds all three columns by catalog update with no heap rewrite, default or backfill, and the brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks touch neither Booking nor Member nor any money, capacity or provider table. WHY WINDOWED. The previous worker ignores all three columns: while a new worker holds a token-fenced lease, an old worker can still select the same unprocessed row, increment attempts without preserving the token, reconcile it, call the email provider, and mark it processed under the pre-fence protocol. Nullable DDL compatibility therefore does not make mixed old/new workers safe. DEPLOY WINDOW. Remove traffic; stop the old web colour and every old worker, scheduler, cron runner and queue consumer; verify no old database connection remains; then set ALLOW_BREAKING_BLUE_GREEN_MIGRATIONS=1, a reason naming the window, and BLUE_GREEN_OLD_APP_AND_WORKERS_STOPPED=1 before validating/migrating. Start new code only. NEW-COLOUR TRANSITION. A NULL re-evaluation token means immediately unclaimed. A pre-existing owner-notification lease from 20260806000000 can have a state key and claimed time but no token; it remains unavailable until its existing 15-minute lease expires, then the new claimant writes a token. DELIVERY CONTRACT. Queue claims are taken just in time, atomically write a fresh token/expiry while incrementing attempts, and completion/failure match the exact token. Notification delivery freezes incident evidence and recipient data only after a final exact incident/state/token read; stale claims make no provider call. Provider calls remain outside transactions, leaving only the documented interval after that final read. ROLLBACK. rollback.sql is deliberately a no-op: stop every NEW worker before starting the old-only release, retain the nullable columns and the applied migration-history row, and let the old client ignore the inert extras so a later new-only roll-forward stays clean. Separately, before any old image starts, prove no AdultMemberHostingPolicy row uses ENFORCED or deliberately reset every such row as documented in DEPLOYMENT.md and docs/PRODUCTION_UPGRADE_RUNBOOK.md. No index, constraint, enum, DML, session-clock expression, backfill or provider call occurs in this migration. Timestamp 20260806010000 is unique and follows 20260806000000.

Adult-member hosting policy (#2364). Purely additive EXPAND in three parts. (1) A NEW table, AdultMemberHostingPolicy, plus the AdultMemberHostingMode enum: created empty, so its deliberately default-less capacityMode (D-R6) needs no backfill and the CREATE TABLE, its unique/plain indexes, its two CHECK constraints and its RESTRICT foreign key to the cold Lodge table lock only objects that did not exist a moment earlier. Two triggers mirror the #2363 policy-set pattern: a BEFORE STATEMENT INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger takes the global hashtext('adult-member-hosting-policy-set') transaction lock before any tuple lock, and a BEFORE ROW INSERT/UPDATE trigger manages the integer revision afterwards. Unlike its #2363 sibling the statement trigger is NOT a drain boundary — this table did not exist before this migration, so no old colour writes it — it exists so that advisory-before-row order holds for every writer including operator DML. (2) Five additive columns on the hot Booking table carrying the hosting review in its OWN state rather than overloading the shared minors-review columns: JSONB adultMemberHostingReview, AdminReviewStatus adultMemberHostingReviewStatus, VARCHAR(500) adultMemberHostingReviewReason, TEXT adultMemberHostingReviewedById and TIMESTAMP(3) adultMemberHostingReviewedAt. All five are nullable with NO default, so PostgreSQL adds them by catalog update with no heap rewrite and no backfill; the single ALTER takes one brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on Booking. adultMemberHostingReviewedById then gains a SET NULL foreign key to Member, matching adminReviewedById and every other actor-attribution column on Booking so member merge repoints it and member deletion nulls it. The constraint is added NOT VALID and VALIDATEd in a second statement: the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock covers only the catalog update, and the validation scan runs under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block booking reads or writes. The column was created empty three statements earlier, so the scan has nothing to check and no existing row can fail it. (3) No index and no data migration at all: nothing in this release queries by hosting review state, so the predicated queue index belongs to #2365 with the query that needs it, and no UPDATE, INSERT or DELETE touches existing rows — no session-clock value is written anywhere. Old-colour forward compatibility: its Prisma client does not know the new table, the new enum or the five new Booking columns, its Booking writes omit them and receive NULL, and it never reads them. New-colour reverse compatibility: bookings the old colour writes during the drain carry a NULL hosting snapshot, which the reconciler reads as "no hosting hazard recorded" and re-derives from live facts the next time the booking is touched. No money, capacity, allocation or provider call is touched. Forward-only expand; rollback would drop the new table, enums and columns and lose only hosting review metadata, returning bookings to the pre-#2364 minors-only review behaviour. Run in the normal deploy window, verify no long-running Booking write transaction is open first, and let the deploy lock timeout stop the brief Booking catalog lock.

Booking-policy exception foundation (#2363). Additive EXPAND only on the cold, admin-sized MinimumStayPolicy table: CREATE TYPE introduces PolicyExceptionCapacityMode with HOLD and NO_HOLD, then one ALTER TABLE adds capacityMode NOT NULL DEFAULT HOLD and integer version NOT NULL DEFAULT 1. PostgreSQL uses the constant defaults to expose HOLD/version 1 for every existing row without a heap rewrite; HOLD is the owner-decided backfill and the capacity default remains only for a draining pre-#2363 colour whose old admin route does not submit the new field. The new runtime requires capacityMode at its API/UI boundary and never relies on the DB default. A BEFORE STATEMENT INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger is the drain compatibility boundary: before any tuple lock, every writer including the old colour takes the exact global `hashtext('minimum-stay-policy-set')` transaction lock, so old and new paths share advisory-before-row order; a separate BEFORE ROW INSERT/UPDATE trigger only manages revisions after that lock is held. Material old-colour updates with an unchanged token advance version once, new-colour OLD+1 updates are not double-incremented, and updatedAt-only/no-op writes do not advance it. MinimumStayPolicy is absent from HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX, but this voluntary row records the compatibility and lock argument. The ALTER and trigger creation take brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE catalog locks on a table containing only club-scale policy rows; no index, FK, provider call, session-clock DML or booking/capacity mutation occurs. Old-colour forward compatibility: its Prisma client ignores both added columns, creates receive safe HOLD/version 1 defaults, and its writes transparently join the new lock/version protocol in PostgreSQL. New-colour reverse compatibility: rows written during the drain still use only the old columns plus these defaulted/trigger-managed scalars, which the old client ignores. Forward-only expand; rollback would remove the triggers/functions and discard only exception review metadata, returning minimum-stay to its former hard-stop-only behaviour. Run in the normal deploy window and let the deploy lock timeout stop the brief catalog lock if the settings table is unexpectedly busy.

Adds the LodgeAccessKind enum, the MemberLodgeAccess grant table, and nullable HutLeaderAssignment.lodgeId backfilled to the sole lodge. Old code ignores the new table and nullable column; HutLeaderAssignment is small and admin-write-only so the ADD COLUMN and backfill locks are brief. Booking eligibility stays default-open until rows exist.
Adds the PromoCodeLodge junction for optional per-lodge promo restrictions. No rows means redeemable at every lodge, so existing promos behave identically; old code ignores the new table entirely.

Loosens CancellationPolicy tier uniqueness from global daysBeforeStay to [lodgeId, daysBeforeStay] so per-lodge override tiers can exist (ADR-001 Q3). Existing rows (all null lodgeId, unique days) satisfy the new index before the old one drops. Old code keeps writing null-lodgeId rows with app-side unique days, so it never violates the new index; nulls being distinct means the database no longer hard-enforces club-wide tier uniqueness — the admin route enforces it in a Serializable replace transaction; the null-partition partial unique index is not added (Prisma cannot express a partial index - see docs/multi-lodge/contract-release.md), so club-wide tier uniqueness stays app-enforced.

Adds the WaitlistCrossLodgeOrder enum, BookingDefaults.waitlistCrossLodgeOrder with default OWN_LODGE_FIRST, nullable Booking.waitlistOfferedLodgeId/waitlistOfferedPriceCents, and the BookingWaitlistAlternateLodge opt-in junction (ADR-004). Old code ignores the new columns and table; the enum column ADD with a default is metadata-only on Postgres 11+ and BookingDefaults is a single-row table, so lock impact is negligible. Cross-lodge offers only happen once new code writes junction rows.

Adds nullable WorkPartyEvent.lodgeId with index and SET NULL FK (lodge-scoping audit 2026-07-03). Null keeps today's meaning — a club-wide working bee bookable at any lodge — so existing rows and old code behave identically; only new code writes or enforces the binding. ADD COLUMN nullable is metadata-only and WorkPartyEvent is a tiny admin-written table.

Adds nullable LodgeInstruction.lodgeId with cascade FK and re-scopes key uniqueness from global to [lodgeId, key] (lodge-scoping audit 2026-07-03). Existing rows (all null lodgeId, unique keys) satisfy the new index before the old one drops; old code reads by key across all rows and only ever sees the club-wide null rows it wrote. Admin writes switch from key-upsert to partition-scoped find/create/update; nulls distinct means the club-wide partition is app-guarded until the contract release partial index, matching the cancellation-policy pattern. Tiny admin-written table; lock impact negligible.

Adds nullable BookingRequest.lodgeId with RESTRICT FK (lodge-scoping audit 2026-07-03). Null keeps meaning the club's default lodge (readers resolve request.lodgeId ?? default), so existing rows and old code behave identically; new requests set it from the public form's lodge choice. Nullable ADD COLUMN is metadata-only; BookingRequest is low-write.

Re-scopes LodgeRoom and Locker name uniqueness from global to [lodgeId, name] so each lodge names its own rooms and lockers (pulled forward from the contract release; the reporter hit "Room 1 already exists" seeding a second lodge). Existing rows are globally unique so they satisfy the composite before the old indexes drop. Old code keeps writing lodge-stamped rows and its own club-wide pre-checks, so it never attempts the cross-lodge duplicates the new index now allows; nulls-distinct means null-lodge rows lose DB-level uniqueness, so app checks treat null rows as clashing at every lodge until the contract release enforces NOT NULL. Index swap on small admin-written tables; lock impact negligible.

Guardedly rewraps only the untouched starter FAQ PageContent row from flat h3/p pairs into native details/summary accordion markup. Admin-edited rows are left unchanged; old code renders the same sanitised HTML as plain content.

Adds a default-false ClubModuleSettings boolean for consent-gated Google Analytics. Old code ignores the column, existing admin-saved module rows keep prior settings, and analytics remains disabled until a new runtime, measurement id, admin opt-in, and visitor consent are all present.

Guardedly updates only the untouched starter Privacy PageContent row to describe optional consent-gated GA4. Admin-edited privacy pages are left unchanged; old code renders the same sanitised HTML as plain content.

Adds new AccessRole enum values for read-only admin, booking officer, membership officer, and content manager bundles. Existing rows are unchanged and full admin remains AccessRole.ADMIN. Do not assign the new enum values until the new runtime is serving traffic, because old Prisma clients may not understand newly written enum values.

Creates the empty TwoFactorSessionChallenge table with a foreign key to Member(id). The FK takes a brief lock on Member to validate the constraint but scans and rewrites no existing rows (new table only). Old code ignores the new table; run during low membership-admin traffic.

Adds nullable LodgeSettings.schoolGroupSoftCap so the school-group soft cap (a warning threshold, previously the hardcoded SCHOOL_GROUP_SOFT_CAP constant) becomes per-lodge configurable. Null falls back to the code default, so existing rows and old code behave identically; nullable ADD COLUMN is metadata-only and LodgeSettings is a tiny admin-written table.

Drops and recreates the two BookingGuest/Booking stay-range envelope triggers as DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint triggers. Takes a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on Booking and BookingGuest to swap the triggers but scans and rewrites no rows. Old code stays compatible because the same cross-table invariant is now checked at COMMIT instead of per-row. Run during low booking-write traffic.

Creates the AccessRoleDefinition table, seeds the six editable default bundles with matrices identical to the legacy hardcoded ones, makes MemberAccessRole.role nullable, and adds a roleDefinitionId FK backfilled for existing enum rows. Old code keeps reading the role enum and behaves identically. Do not create or assign custom (NULL-role) definitions until the new runtime is fully serving traffic, because old Prisma clients select role as non-nullable and can error on NULL-role rows.

Adds default-true BookingDefaults and BookingPeriod booleans for member-priority non-member holds, preserving existing Members First behavior until an admin disables it. Guardedly refreshes only untouched starter Terms/FAQ PageContent copy; admin-edited rows are left unchanged. Old code ignores the new columns and continues treating holds as enabled.

Enforces NOT NULL on lodgeId for LodgeRoom, Locker, Season, ChoreTemplate, HutLeaderAssignment, and Booking. old_code_compatible via a default_lodge_id() column DEFAULT set in the SAME migration: an old (pre-lodge) colour's INSERT omits lodgeId and receives the default lodge, so no null is written and NOT NULL holds throughout a blue/green cutover - no outage, no migration abort. The default is kept permanently (harmless; new code always stamps lodgeId explicitly and it only fires for an old colour's omitted-column writes). Booking is hot but the column is fully populated (expand backfill + writer-stamping), so SET NOT NULL is a validation scan, not a rewrite; take the brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock during low booking traffic. The validator recognises the SET NOT NULL + same-column SET DEFAULT pattern as old-code-compatible, so this deploys without ALLOW_BREAKING_BLUE_GREEN_MIGRATIONS.

Single UPDATE flipping ADULT organisation-type members (legacy SCHOOL role or ORG access role) to the new NOT_APPLICABLE AgeTier value; touches only those rows (typically a handful per club) with brief row locks and no DDL. CAUTION: pre-#1440 Prisma clients cannot deserialize NOT_APPLICABLE, so old-color reads of the flipped rows (admin members list, that member's detail, school flows) can error between migrate and cutover — deploy in a quiet window and cut over promptly, or defer this migration until the old color drains (the UPDATE is idempotent and safe to run late).

Two idempotent single-row UPDATEs repairing the 20260708000000 lodge seed's createdAt/updatedAt, which were written with session-time CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and render NZ local time (~12-13h ahead of UTC) on non-UTC databases (the shipped compose sets PGTZ=Pacific/Auckland), letting a same-day app-created lodge sort earlier and silently become the club default (#1627). Clamps a future-skewed seed timestamp to UTC now, then restores the seeded lodge (slug 'lodge') as the strictly-earliest row when another lodge sorts at-or-before it. No-op on UTC databases and single-lodge installs; touches at most one row; old code unaffected (nothing reads absolute createdAt values - only the relative ordering both colours already expect).

Drops the retired MemberInductionItemResult table and the InductionItemResultValue enum after the single-Pass induction flow stopped recording per-item results. Retired at the code level by 20260702100000_induction_workflow_types; no deployed runtime reads or writes this table (no src/ readers or writers remain), so old app colours stay compatible during the blue/green window. Production holds zero rows (verified 2026-07-08, evidence on #1532), so the drop loses no data. DROP TABLE takes a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on this empty, unreferenced leaf table with no row-validation scan, then DROP TYPE removes the now-unused enum; MemberInduction* are low-write induction tables, not hot tables. Run during low induction/membership-admin traffic.

Drops the retired MemberInduction.selfAssessedAt and selfAssessmentJson columns. 20260702100000_induction_workflow_types NULLed all in-flight values and removed every app-level read/write, and the production retention check on 2026-07-08 confirmed zero non-NULL values across all 4 rows (evidence on #1532), so no data is lost and DROP COLUMN is a metadata-only catalog update (no rewrite, no row scan, brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock; MemberInduction is not a hot table). RESIDUAL WINDOW (owner-accepted 2026-07-08, single-release disposition per #1533): the previously deployed colour's Prisma client still names both columns in its default SELECT/RETURNING lists, so between migrate and cutover the old colour errors on the default-selection induction paths (induction.ts create/update RETURNING and findUnique/findFirst/findMany includes, plus the admin inductions list) - reads AND create/update writes on inductions fail with column-does-not-exist until cutover; paths with explicit selects and counts are unaffected. Induction traffic is near-nil (4 rows total in production), so deploy in a quiet window, cut over promptly (or drain the old colour first), and use ALLOW_BREAKING_BLUE_GREEN_MIGRATIONS=1 with that acknowledgement as the override reason - same pattern as the 20260526120000 and 20260708220300 rows.

Contract drop of the value-dead sectionLabel/lineLabel columns and their composite index on FinanceReportCategoryMapping. previous_expand_release names 20260629000000_add_finance_report_category_subtype, the RUNTIME release (PR #938) that removed text-label P&L fallback matching so the app logic has ignored these columns VALUES since; policy prose permits naming the runtime release. WRITES are unaffected (createMany inserts accountCode only, no RETURNING of dropped columns). Impact is admin-only, read-only, brief and retryable. old_code_compatible=yes is asserted in the promo-redesign sense (20260526120000): deploy only with old traffic idle or routed to the new runtime, and use the ALLOW_BREAKING override only with that operator acknowledgement (prefer a low-traffic window). Not a hot table (absent from HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX; neither table nor index name matches); DROP COLUMN is a metadata-only catalog change taking a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and the preceding DROP INDEX likewise. Zero data loss: read-only production count on #1532 found 31 rows with no non-NULL label values.

Expand-only CREATE TABLE for MemberCreditNoteAllocation (per-note applied-credit allocation lots, #1620) plus its indexes and unique key; no existing table or column is touched. Flagged by the hot-table regex only because the new table declares a single FK REFERENCES "MemberCredit" (appliedToBookingId is a bare scalar with no Booking FK, by design) - creating an empty table with one FK takes only a brief ROW SHARE lock on the referenced table with no validation scan (zero rows) and no rewrite. Old-colour compatibility is total: the previously deployed client has no model for this table and never reads or writes it; only the new APPLIED_CREDIT_ALLOCATION engine references it. No backfill: pre-existing floating credit notes correctly read as fully unallocated (zero rows = full remaining balance by construction). Safe at any traffic level.

Expand-only ADD COLUMN of the nullable MemberCredit.restoredFromBookingId dedupe key plus its unique index (#1636). The nullable ADD COLUMN (no default) is a metadata-only catalog change taking a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock with no table rewrite and no row scan. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX scans MemberCredit to build the index, but the column is brand-new and all-NULL so no uniqueness conflict is possible and the build is fast; MemberCredit is a low/medium-write finance-history table, not a hot booking-path table. Flagged by the hot-table regex only because ALTER TABLE / the ON clause name "MemberCredit". Old-colour compatibility is total: the previously deployed Prisma client has no model field for this column and never reads or writes it (only restoreCreditFromBooking sets it, in the new colour); nullable + all-NULL existing rows satisfy the unique index during the migrate->cutover window. Safe at any traffic level; prefer a low-write window for the index build on very large ledgers.

Adds raw-SQL partial unique indexes over the club-wide (lodgeId IS NULL) partitions of CancellationPolicy (daysBeforeStay) and LodgeInstruction (key), closing the multi-lodge contract-release deferral: PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct under the composite [lodgeId, ...] uniques, so these partitions were app-enforced only. Neither table is hot and no breaking SQL is present; this row exists for documentation, like the multi_lodge_entity_lodge_id_not_null row. A defensive dedupe DELETE precedes each index build (keep greatest updatedAt then id per duplicate group) so a lost-race duplicate can never abort the deploy; app enforcement (Serializable replace transaction / findFirst-then-write) should make it a no-op, and any row it removes is an invisible-duplicate bug state, not user-visible data. Both are small config tables, so the DELETE self-join scan and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX build are brief (brief SHARE lock on writes during each index build; reads unaffected). Old-colour compatibility is total: old code enforces the same uniqueness app-side, so the indexes reject nothing an old colour legitimately writes. Drift-gate note: prisma migrate diff does not surface partial indexes (Member_email_primary_unique / Member_email_login_unique / XeroSyncOperation precedents), so db:check-drift stays green.

Contract drop of the EmailMessageSetting legacy lodge-identity columns (lodgeName, lodgeTravelNote, doorCode) after this same release refactors email identity resolution to always read from Lodge (default lodge when no lodgeId is in scope), retiring syncSoleActiveLodgeIdentity. Single-release disposition per the 20260708220100/20260708220200/20260708220300 precedent. OLD-CODE CAVEAT: the previously deployed colour's Prisma client still names the three columns in its default SELECT/RETURNING lists on the singleton, so between migrate and cutover: member-facing email sends DEGRADE but do not fail (loadPersistedEmailMessageSettings catches the error and falls back to config defaults, and per-booking lodge identity already reads from Lodge on that colour), while the admin email-settings GET/PUT and the lodge-admin create/update routes (whose transactions call the retired sync upsert) error with column-does-not-exist until cutover - admin-only, brief, retryable. Zero data loss: the migration first backfills the default lodge's travelNote/doorCode from the singleton where the Lodge values are NULL (default_lodge_id() as replaced by 20260709120000: isDefault flag first, else oldest active, else oldest - matching the app's getDefaultLodgeId and this release's email resolveLodgeIdentity); Lodge.name is NOT NULL and authoritative so a divergent email-only lodgeName is superseded by design. EmailMessageSetting is a single-row config table (not in HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX); the backfill touches at most one Lodge row and DROP COLUMN is a metadata-only catalog change with a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. Deploy in a quiet window with old traffic idle or drained and use ALLOW_BREAKING_BLUE_GREEN_MIGRATIONS=1 with that acknowledgement as the override reason.

Idempotent data repair (#1665): four action-scoped UPDATEs rewrite plaintext door codes in historical AuditLog metadata to the '[set]' redaction convention that PR #1663 established going forward. Covered: LODGE_CREATED/LODGE_UPDATED/LODGE_ACTIVATED/LODGE_DEACTIVATED newLodge/previousLodge.doorCode (the [id] route emits all three update-family actions with the same metadata shape, unredacted from the multi-lodge release until #1663), plus EMAIL_MESSAGE_SETTINGS_UPDATED previousSettings/newSettings.doorCode purely defensively (its redactor shipped in the same commit as the field, so plaintext rows are not expected; the statements are shape-guarded no-ops). The columns themselves were dropped by 20260709130000; this touches only audit history. Shape-guarded jsonb_set: only JSON string values other than '[set]' change, JSON nulls keep recording that no code was set, and re-running is a no-op. No data loss beyond the deliberate secret removal; whether a code existed remains recorded. No DDL; AuditLog is not in HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX; the UPDATEs use the indexed action column and take brief row locks on matching admin-audit rows only. Old-colour compatibility is total (both colours only read metadata for display; the value shape stays a JSON string). Safe at any traffic level; this row exists for documentation like the 20260708220000 metadata-only precedent.

Idempotent data-only correction (#1832) of the singleton default ClubTheme row from the legacy generic sage palette to the current generic teal defaults. The single UPDATE is guarded by id='default', completedAt IS NULL, and an exact match on every stored legacy theme value after the earlier #1244 gold bump (all seven colours, both fonts, NULL logo, and empty raw CSS), so completed, partially customized, Tokoroa, and non-default themes are untouched. Consolidates the six never-shipped lobby-display feature-branch migrations (schema, name granularity, device templateKey, notice, authoring v2, poll seconds) into ONE expand migration, per ADR-003 and issue #86 (LTV-040) which re-layers the branch onto clean history before the single upstream PR. DisplayLayout/DisplayTemplate/LodgeDisplayDevice are absent from HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX and Lodge/ClubModuleSettings gain only additive columns. old_code_compatible=yes: the previously deployed colour has no Prisma model field for any of these tables, columns or the boolean and never reads or writes them (the lobbyDisplay module flag defaults OFF and no production club has enabled it, so the feature never shipped). Any staging/dev database that applied the superseded migrations must be reset with a fresh migrate deploy — the documented ADR-003 clean-slate plan for this unshipped branch; this migration never runs against a production blue/green window. Expand-only additive ADD COLUMN of Member.lodgeScreenPhoneOptIn and Lodge.showGuestPhonesOnScreens (both BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false), the two-sided phone-visibility opt-in for lodge screens (#37/#124). Additive fee-authority migration (#1855): creates two new schedule tables/enums and btree_gist exclusion constraints; adds nullable public-copy/listing fields and FamilyGroup.billingMembershipId, a Prisma-representable SET NULL FK to the selected FamilyGroupMember row. The API accepts a member ID only after resolving an active, unarchived membership in the same family; deleting that join row clears the recipient automatically. The public flag has a constant false default (PG16 catalog-only); the nullable FamilyGroup column is metadata-only. Index/FK creation briefly locks the cold FamilyGroup/FamilyGroupMember configuration tables and validates only an all-NULL new column, so no existing-row failure is possible. Entrance backfill reads small Xero mapping tables only, validates legacy text/range before integer cast, writes explicit UTC updatedAt values, and derives the effective date from statement time in Pacific/Auckland. Old code ignores all additions and continues using retained mapping amounts; new code is schedule-first with one-release fallback. No provider calls, destructive SQL, hot-row rewrite, or old-colour incompatibility.

Additive subscription-billing migration (#1857): creates new enums and cold workflow/settings/snapshot/coverage/exception tables only. Existing Member and MemberSubscription rows are not rewritten; no existing table receives a required column. Unique indexes and checks protect immutable charge identity, one charge per subscription, one charge per family/membership-type/year, integer-cent/non-negative amounts, inclusive-month bounds, due-day bounds, and zero-cent NO_INVOICE snapshots; nullable account/item columns freeze provider mapping only on new invoice charges. Expand-only additive migration for the exclusive whole-lodge hold (#116/#117, ADR-001): ADD COLUMN Booking.wholeLodgeHold (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false), Booking.wholeLodgeHoldAt (nullable), Booking.wholeLodgeHoldByMemberId (nullable), and BookingRequest.exclusivityRequested (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false). Adds a plain (non-CONCURRENT) index Booking_wholeLodgeHoldByMemberId_idx and an FK to Member(id) ON DELETE SET NULL: the index build takes a SHARE lock blocking Booking writes for its (all-null, fast) build, and ADD CONSTRAINT validates existing rows (all null, trivially valid) under a brief lock — both acceptable at this table's size; switch to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY if Booking grows large. Flagged by the hot-table regex only because ALTER TABLE names Booking. No backfill. Capacity enforcement is deferred to #118.

Run in the normal deploy window; the ADD COLUMN is metadata-only and the index/FK builds are on a cold club-scale table with an empty FK validation set, so let the deploy guard stop on lock timeout.

Custodian bed hold — a bed held for a season by a hut-leader assignment, with no booking (#2286, epic #2245). Additive EXPAND only, three statements, both tables COLD. (1) ALTER TABLE "HutLeaderAssignment" ADD COLUMN "bedId" TEXT — nullable with NO default, so it is a PostgreSQL catalog-only add (no table rewrite, no row scan) taking a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on a table holding at most a few rows per lodge per season. (2) CREATE INDEX "HutLeaderAssignment_bedId_idx" — a plain btree over an all-NULL column on that same cold table. (3) ALTER TABLE "HutLeaderAssignment" ADD CONSTRAINT "HutLeaderAssignment_bedId_fkey" REFERENCES "LodgeBed"("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT — every existing row has bedId NULL, so the validation scan matches nothing, and the referenced LodgeBed table is likewise cold (tens of rows per lodge). Neither "HutLeaderAssignment" nor "LodgeBed" appears in HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX in scripts/validate-blue-green-migrations.sh, and none of the three statements matches its breaking-statement regex, so THE BLUE/GREEN GATE IS SILENT FOR THIS MIGRATION BY DESIGN — this voluntary ledger row is the only audit trail, which is why it is written with full reasoning rather than as a formality. No enum change, no DROP TABLE/COLUMN/TYPE/CONSTRAINT, no RENAME, no ALTER COLUMN TYPE/SET NOT NULL on existing data, no backfill DML, no session-clock write, and no Xero/Stripe/SES/AI provider call runs in-migration. The migration deliberately does not restate HutLeaderAssignment."lodgeId"'s dbgenerated default_lodge_id() default. Old-colour compatible: the previously deployed Prisma client has no bedId field on HutLeaderAssignment and no custodianHolds relation on LodgeBed, so it never selects, filters on, or writes the column; every existing and old-colour-created row is NULL, and NULL is exactly the pre-#2286 semantics (an assignment without a bed is a role only, with zero capacity effect — including every row cron-hut-leader-auto-assign.ts creates, which never sets bedId). The one accepted drain-window exposure runs the other way: between migrate and cutover a new-colour admin can create a custodian hold on a bed, and the OLD colour's bed-allocation write paths (manual single-night, bulk, board move, run-auto-allocation) carry no custodian check, so an old-colour admin could allocate a guest onto that held bed for the seconds-to-minutes of the drain. It is admin-only, produces no data corruption (the BedAllocation row is ordinary and removable), never reaches a member-facing surface, and self-surfaces: the new colour's board raises a CUSTODIAN_BED_CONFLICT warning for any allocation row overlapping a hold, so the drain-window collision is visible and fixable on the board immediately after cutover. Accepted rather than choreographed, because the alternative (representing the hold as nullable-FK BedAllocation rows) would break the old colour on a runtime-hot table. Forward-only expand (no automated rollback needed): dropping the column on rollback only discards which bed each custodian holds, leaving the assignments themselves intact and the lodge back to full bookable capacity. Run in the normal deploy window; every lock here is brief and on a cold table, so let the deploy guard stop on lock timeout.

Member-guest module flag + policy singleton ("+ Add Member Guest", #2306, epic #2305). Additive EXPAND: cold catalog-only ADD COLUMN DEFAULT plus one brand-new cold table; expand-safe. ALTER TABLE "ClubModuleSettings" ADD COLUMN "memberGuests" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false — a PostgreSQL metadata-only add with a constant default (no table rewrite, no row scan) on the cold single-row ClubModuleSettings catalog singleton, taking a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock; ClubModuleSettings is absent from HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX. CREATE TABLE "MemberGuestSettings" (the id="default" policy singleton: approvalRequired, pendingHoldExpiryDays, openMemberSearchEnabled, openMemberSearchIncludesMinors, updatedByMemberId, timestamps) plus the plain btree index "MemberGuestSettings_updatedByMemberId_idx" — a brand-new empty table, so the CREATE TABLE + index lock touches nothing, and it carries NO foreign key (updatedByMemberId is deliberately a bare column, the same shape as BookingRequestSettings.updatedByMemberId), so nothing here references Member and the FK case of HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX is not tripped. No enum change, no DROP TABLE/COLUMN/TYPE/CONSTRAINT, no RENAME, no ALTER COLUMN TYPE/SET NOT NULL on existing data, no backfill DML, no session-clock write, and no Xero/Stripe/SES/provider call runs in-migration. NO settings row is seeded: the singleton is created lazily on the first WRITE — a read materialises nothing, it synthesises the schema defaults on a miss — so the session-clock DML gate has nothing to catch. Old-colour compatible: the previously deployed Prisma client has no MemberGuestSettings model (never reads/writes the new table) and reads ClubModuleSettings only through CLUB_MODULE_SETTINGS_COLUMN_SELECT, which does not name the new column, so the added flag is invisible to it and defaults false. The new-colour runtime is the sole reader/writer, and in THIS release the flag is inert in the sense that matters here: no booking path reads it, so turning memberGuests on changes no outcome at any of the seven resolveLinkedBookingMembers call sites (the cross-family refusal is gated on MEMBER_GUEST_WIDENING_ENABLED, which is false), and an admin therefore cannot create state the old colour would not understand. The one thing it does change is the admin Modules card, which reports "Not available yet" instead of "Enabled" (D-17) — a new-colour-only surface the old colour never renders. Forward-only expand (no automated rollback needed): dropping the table/column on rollback only discards an inert flag and inert policy values. Run in the normal deploy window; the CREATE TABLE + index locks are on a brand-new empty table and the single metadata-only ADD COLUMN takes a brief lock on the cold catalog table, so let the deploy guard stop on lock timeout.

Member-guest consent columns on BookingGuest ("+ Add Member Guest", #2306, epic #2305, owner decision D-7). Additive EXPAND only, on a HOT table. (1) CREATE TYPE "MemberGuestConsentStatus" AS ENUM ('PENDING','CONFIRMED','DECLINED','EXPIRED') — a brand-new enum type. The partial index in (4) DOES name one of its labels ('PENDING'), so this is NOT a "registers the labels and never uses one" migration, and it does not need to be: what PostgreSQL forbids is using a label added by ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE inside the transaction that added it, whereas a type introduced by CREATE TYPE is usable immediately in that same transaction. Prisma's per-migration transaction is therefore safe here. (20260525000000 / 20260719130000 / 20260720130000 / 20260727120000 are the ALTER TYPE case, which is precisely why those migrations never use the label they add.) The narrower claim that carries the blue/green argument does hold unchanged: no DML and no column default names a label, so no ROW ever carries one as a result of this migration. (2) ALTER TABLE "BookingGuest" ADD COLUMN "consentStatus" "MemberGuestConsentStatus", "consentRequestedAt"/"consentRespondedAt"/"consentExpiresAt" TIMESTAMP(3), "consentRespondedByMemberId" TEXT — every one nullable with NO default, so each is a PostgreSQL catalog-only add (no table rewrite, no row scan, no backfill) taking a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on BookingGuest, which IS in HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX, hence this row. (3) NO foreign key on consentRespondedByMemberId: it is deliberately a bare column, the same choice (and for the same reason) as BookingGuest.rateMembershipTypeId — an FK here would add a validating constraint on this hot table AND take a lock on Member, and the audit value must survive even when the recorded approver is later deleted. So there is no ADD CONSTRAINT, no validation scan, and no Member lock anywhere in this migration. (4) CREATE INDEX "BookingGuest_pendingConsent_expiresAt_idx" ON "BookingGuest" ("consentExpiresAt") WHERE "consentStatus" = 'PENDING' — a plain (non-CONCURRENT) partial btree index for MG2's expiry sweep, built here deliberately while the predicate matches ZERO rows: the columns were added moments earlier and nothing in this release can write a non-null consentStatus, so the index it writes is EMPTY. Two costs, stated as they are rather than optimistically. (i) LOCK DURATION: Prisma runs the whole migration file in ONE transaction, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock the first ADD COLUMN takes on BookingGuest is held until COMMIT — through the index build — rather than being released and re-taken as a briefer SHARE lock for the CREATE INDEX. The window in which BookingGuest writers block is the whole migration, not each statement in turn. (ii) BUILD COST: an empty result is not a free build. Creating a predicated index still scans the entire heap of BookingGuest to evaluate the predicate row by row, so the cost is proportional to the table, not to the zero matches. Both are acceptable at this table's size (club-scale, a handful of rows per booking) in the normal deploy window, with the deploy guard's lock timeout as the backstop. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY is NOT the escape hatch that sentence used to promise: PostgreSQL forbids it inside a transaction block and Prisma always wraps a migration in one, so it cannot be used from a Prisma migration at all. If BookingGuest ever grows to where a full heap scan under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE is unacceptable, the index must be built OUT OF BAND (a manual CONCURRENTLY build, still recorded in prisma/partial-unique-indexes.tsv), not by editing the migration. Prisma cannot express a predicated index, so it is invisible to schema.prisma and to db:check-drift and is recorded instead in prisma/partial-unique-indexes.tsv, whose set-equality is enforced by scripts/check-partial-indexes.sh in the migration-drift CI job. Building it now is what lets MG2 (#2307) ship its sweep with no migration of its own. No DROP TABLE/COLUMN/TYPE/CONSTRAINT, no RENAME, no ALTER COLUMN TYPE/SET NOT NULL, no backfill DML, no session-clock write, and no Xero/Stripe/SES/provider call runs in-migration. Old-colour compatible in BOTH directions, and the reverse direction is the important one. Forward: the previously deployed Prisma client has no consent* fields, never selects or writes them, and never names the new enum, so every existing BookingGuest read and write behaves exactly as before with all five columns NULL. Reverse: the risk that dominated the 20260727120000_add_booking_no_emails row -- the NEW colour writing an enum label an OLD-colour Prisma client would reject on read -- was ABSENT while MG1 was the deployed colour and is PRESENT from MG2 (#2307) onward, and this row is deliberately updated rather than left reading as though the dark guarantee still held. MG1 (#2306) shipped the widening behind a hard-coded false, so no code path could write a non-null consentStatus for any actor. MG2 turns the memberGuests module into the real gate, so a club that switches it on WILL carry PENDING / CONFIRMED / DECLINED / EXPIRED rows. What that means operationally: this MIGRATION is still reverse-safe by itself (the columns and the type stay; nothing is dropped), but ROLLING THE APPLICATION back past MG2 while such rows exist would hand a Prisma client that has no MemberGuestConsentStatus enum a column carrying one of its labels. The mitigation is the module flag, not the schema: an operator rolling back must turn the memberGuests module OFF first, which stops new rows, and must expect existing PENDING rows to hold their beds until an MG2-or-later colour runs the expiry sweep again -- there is no released code in an MG1 colour that can resolve or expire them. That is the whole reason MG1 refused to let the module flag mean anything. Recorded here because the previous wording made a claim about the DEPLOYED CODE, not about the migration, and MG2 falsified it; the call-site census it rested on is unchanged and still worth stating: through any of the seven resolveLinkedBookingMembers call sites (SIX of the seven can pass skipAuthorization: true -- admin-booking-copy hard-codes it, booking-modify-plan passes role === "ADMIN", the guests and modify-quote routes pass isAdmin, and the create and quote routes pass isAuthorizedOnBehalf; only the group-booking join can never skip). The labels are registered a full release before the code that can write one, which is exactly the "ship the enum value one release ahead" mitigation that row recommended. Forward-only expand (no automated rollback needed): dropping the columns, the enum type, and the partial index on rollback discards only inert, all-NULL consent state. Run in the normal deploy window; the ADD COLUMNs are metadata-only and the partial index build writes an empty index (though it still heap-scans BookingGuest, under a lock held for the whole file), so let the deploy guard stop on lock timeout.

Data repair so a promo redemption that delivered NO benefit stops consuming usage caps (#2299, owner decision recorded on the issue; binding). PURE DML, phase metadata-only: no DDL at all -- no CREATE/ALTER/DROP of any table, column, type, index, constraint or foreign key, no RENAME, no SET NOT NULL, no enum change, no session-clock write (neither statement names CURRENT_TIMESTAMP or now(); "updatedAt" is deliberately left untouched because this is a system repair, not an admin edit), and no Xero/Stripe/SES/provider call runs in-migration. Two statements, both on tables ABSENT from HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX in scripts/validate-blue-green-migrations.sh, and neither matching its BREAKING_SQL_REGEX or DESTRUCTIVE_REMOVAL_SQL_REGEX (a row DELETE is not a DROP), so THE BLUE/GREEN GATE IS SILENT FOR THIS MIGRATION BY DESIGN -- this voluntary ledger row is the only audit trail, which is why it is written with full reasoning rather than as a formality. (1) DELETE FROM "PromoRedemptionAllocation" WHERE "discountCents" <= 0 AND "priceAdjustmentCents" = 0 AND "freeNightsUsed" <= 0 -- removes the historical all-zero allocation rows the pre-#2299 code force-wrote whenever a promo had eligible guests but computed no benefit. The predicate is the exact negation of the applications benefit test (isBeneficialPromoAllocation / BENEFICIAL_PROMO_ALLOCATION_FILTER in src/lib/promo.ts), so code and migration can never disagree about which rows count. The statement takes ROW locks on the matched rows plus a brief ROW EXCLUSIVE table lock on PromoRedemptionAllocation (which does NOT block concurrent reads or unrelated writes); the table is club-scale (at most one row per beneficiary per promo application) and the matched set is expected to be a handful of rows, or zero on a healthy install. No cascade fans out of it: PromoRedemptionAllocation is a leaf -- nothing references it -- so deleting a row touches Booking, Member, PromoRedemption and PromoCode not at all, and in particular NO PromoRedemption row is removed. That is the point: the redemption row stays as the audit and reporting trail, and only what counts as a *use* changes. (2) UPDATE "PromoCode" SET "currentRedemptions" = <count of that codes surviving allocation rows> WHERE the two differ -- rebases the denormalised total-redemptions counter, which a query filter cannot fix. Written as a correlated recount rather than a decrement so it is IDEMPOTENT (re-running is a no-op) and so it also repairs any counter that had already drifted for an unrelated reason. The WHERE ... <> clause means untouched codes are not written at all. Locks: brief ROW EXCLUSIVE on PromoCode plus row locks on the codes that actually change; PromoCode holds tens of rows at club scale. Old-colour compatible, and the direction of every difference is the safe one. The previously deployed Prisma client reads exactly the same columns and models -- nothing is added or removed for it to trip over -- so the only thing it observes is smaller numbers: fewer allocation rows and a lower (correct) "currentRedemptions". For the old colour that is strictly MORE PERMISSIVE: a member whose only prior application of a code delivered nothing is no longer told "You have already used this promo code", and a code whose total-redemptions cap looked exhausted by benefit-free applications becomes usable again. Both are precisely the intended fix arriving a few minutes early for the draining colour, not a regression -- and it can never over-discount, because the discount maths is untouched; only the eligibility counting changes. The reverse direction during the migrate->cutover drain is bounded and self-healing: an OLD-colour pod can still create a fresh all-zero allocation row and increment "currentRedemptions" by one for it -- either by writing one itself, or via the pre-existing PromoRedemption_sync_allocation_insert/_update triggers from 20260527120000_add_promo_redemption_allocations, which upsert a booker allocation row from a redemption's own scalars on every PromoRedemption write (those triggers are DELIBERATELY LEFT IN PLACE by this migration: they are the mechanism that keeps an old colour's redemptions visible as allocations, and the new colour neutralises them by deleting the redemption's allocation rows immediately AFTER each PromoRedemption create/update and before writing its own beneficial set). The new colour filters such a row out of every cap count immediately (per-member, unique-member, and the member-facing status all query with the benefit filter, so the query-filter half of the fix covers it without waiting for anything), leaving only the denormalised counter one too HIGH for that code -- i.e. drifted in the CONSERVATIVE direction, blocking a use slightly early rather than allowing one too many. It is CORRECTABLE BY RE-RUNNING THE MIGRATION DML, and this is the only residual step the migration leaves behind: OPERATOR ACTION -- after the cutover completes and the old colour has fully drained, re-run both statements once (both are idempotent, statement (2) is a correlated recount rather than a decrement, so a re-run on a clean install is a no-op). Do NOT rely on the drift clearing itself: it only clears if that particular booking is later repriced or removed, because the counter writers measure their delta against the RAW allocation row count and so give back exactly what was taken -- a booking that is never touched again keeps its trigger-written all-zero row, and its code's counter, one too high permanently. Conservative direction throughout: one use blocked early, never one allowed extra. ONE EXCEPTION runs the other way, and only during the drain: the sync triggers never write "priceAdjustmentCents" -- not on INSERT (it takes DEFAULT 0) and not in their ON CONFLICT set-list -- so a PRICE-RAISING fixed-nightly (SET_PRICE) redemption written by an old colour, which has discountCents = 0, freeNightsUsed = 0 and priceAdjustmentCents > 0, produces an ALL-ZERO trigger row. The new colour reads that row as non-beneficial, so a use the new definition counts consumes no cap, and re-running the repair would delete the row rather than fix it. The trigger is deliberately NOT changed here (it is legacy blue/green compatibility, due for removal with the triggers themselves, and altering it during a drain is the riskier act); the exposure is one narrow promo type, only for redemptions written inside the drain window, and it UNDER-counts a cap rather than over-charging anyone -- no member is ever billed for it. Forward-only (no automated rollback needed, and none is meaningful): the deleted rows carried no benefit and no money -- every one of them had zero discount, zero price adjustment and zero free nights -- so nothing recoverable is lost, and the counter can be recomputed from the surviving rows at any time by re-running statement (2). Run in the normal deploy window; both statements are short DML on cold club-scale tables and take no ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, so nothing blocks concurrent readers and the deploy guard has nothing to stop on.

Additional-payment chase stamps (#2350). Additive EXPAND only, on a HOT table. ONE ALTER TABLE "Payment" with two ADD COLUMNs — "additionalReminderSentAt" and "additionalFinalReminderSentAt", both TIMESTAMP(3), both nullable with NO default — so each is a PostgreSQL catalog-only add (no table rewrite, no row scan, no backfill) and the statement takes a single brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on "Payment" for the catalog write only. "Payment" IS in HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX, hence this row. No enum change, no index, no constraint, no foreign key, no DROP TABLE/COLUMN/TYPE/CONSTRAINT, no RENAME, no ALTER COLUMN TYPE/SET NOT NULL, no backfill DML, no session-clock write, and no Xero/Stripe/SES/provider call runs in-migration. Every existing row is left NULL, which is exactly the "nobody has been chased about this delta yet" state the new reminder cron reads, so no data migration exists to get wrong. The two columns are pure send-bookkeeping: they record WHEN the member was last emailed about an outstanding additional payment and never carry money, so no figure anywhere is derived from them. Old-colour compatible in BOTH directions. Forward: the previously deployed Prisma client has no additionalReminderSentAt / additionalFinalReminderSentAt fields, never selects or writes them, and has no reminder that consults them, so every existing Payment read and write behaves exactly as before. Reverse: a stamp written by the NEW colour during the migrate->cutover drain is a plain timestamp the old colour ignores entirely (it neither selects nor asserts on it); the worst case is that an old-colour process cannot see that a reminder already went out, and since the old colour has no additional-payment reminder of its own to send, nothing can double-send. The stamps are also read RELATIVE to the current additional-payment episode (the latest ADDITIONAL PaymentTransaction createdAt), never as plain booleans, so a stamp left behind by an earlier, already-settled delta cannot suppress the chase for a later one and no writer has to reset them. Forward-only expand (no automated rollback needed): dropping the columns on rollback discards only the record of which reminders were sent, so the chase sequence restarts from the beginning for any still-owing delta — an extra email, never a lost or double-collected payment. Run in the normal deploy window; the two metadata-only ADD COLUMNs take a brief lock on "Payment", so let the deploy guard stop on lock timeout.

Idempotent data repair (#2269, epic #2245 lane 3 F3): ONE statement strips the square-bracketed authoring notes this project used to ship inside its email default bodies out of every saved EmailTemplateOverride, and writes one actorless EMAIL_TEMPLATE_OVERRIDE_UPDATED AuditLog row per mutated row carrying the whole before/after and the exact spans removed. No DDL. MATCHES 38 EXACT STRINGS, NOT A PATTERN FAMILY: the alternation in the "annotation" CTE is byte-identical to SHIPPED_ANNOTATION_PATTERN in src/lib/email-message-token-contract.ts (asserted by src/lib/__tests__/email-message-annotation-strip.test.ts, which also rebuilds the six pass patterns from this file and runs the corpus through them). An earlier prefix-family draft was reproduced deleting club-authored prose ("Ring the lodge [when you are 30 minutes away]."), which is unrecoverable in-product because the editor refuses to save square brackets, so the rule was narrowed to literal strings; the accepted cost is that a re-spaced or retyped note is NOT healed and keeps surfacing in the #2320 bracket banner for an admin to resolve. Both tables are COLD - EmailTemplateOverride holds at most one row per registered template and is read once per send, AuditLog is append-only - so no lock-impact window is needed and it runs in the ordinary deploy window. Neither table appears in HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX in scripts/validate-blue-green-migrations.sh and no statement matches its breaking-statement regex, so THE BLUE/GREEN GATE IS SILENT FOR THIS MIGRATION BY DESIGN and this voluntary row is the only audit trail. NO SESSION-CLOCK WRITE: every timestamp this statement writes is timezone('UTC', statement_timestamp()) - "updatedAt", "expiresAt", and "createdAt", which is NAMED EXPLICITLY in the AuditLog insert. Left unnamed it would take the column default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, i.e. the SESSION's local wall clock into a naive timestamp(3) column, measured 12 hours out on a Pacific/Auckland session - the #1627/#1656 class, which the session-clock gate does not catch when the clock hides in a column default. Metadata timestamps use to_char(...'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') so they parse as instants in JavaScript rather than as local time. CONCURRENCY-SAFE WITH THE OLD COLOUR STILL SERVING: the audit INSERT selects FROM the UPDATE's RETURNING, and the UPDATE re-checks "subject"/"bodyText" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM the values the strip was computed from, so a concurrent admin Save is never clobbered and a concurrent Restore Default (DELETE) produces no audit row for a template that no longer exists. Both cases were reproduced against postgres:16 before the fix and verified after. AUDIT METADATA IS DELIBERATELY NOT SANITIZED: SQL has no access to sanitizeAuditMetadata, so the 1000-char truncation, 24 KB envelope cap and secret/card redaction are all skipped. Verbatim storage is required - a truncated copy could not restore a club's wording - but it means a club that typed a LITERAL door code into its body instead of {{doorCode}} now has it in an unredacted row retained 7 years (cf. 20260710000100_redact_audit_log_door_codes). Blast radius is bounded by the save route's 500/10,000-character caps. Called out in docs/UPGRADING.md for operators. The APP's own Restore Default path now archives its deleted copy at the same fidelity (src/app/api/admin/email-templates/reset/route.ts asks buildStructuredAuditLogCreateArgs for archiveText mode, which relaxes the 1000-char clip and the long-HTML placeholder while still applying secret, card-number and sensitive-key redaction), so the two halves of #2269 no longer disagree about how much of the same content they keep. THESE AUDIT ROWS ARE NOW READ BY THE APPLICATION, not only by an operator: the admin email-templates GET filters AuditLog on action + entityType + metadata->>'source' = this migration's id and derives the editor's stripped_annotation reason from previousOverride/removedAnnotations, because the bracket WAS the conditional marker and a conditional line with no {{token}} in it ("Payment has been processed successfully. [only when the booking is already paid]", ten such lines across the historical defaults) has no other signal once the bracket is gone. Deleting or rewriting these rows therefore silences a member-facing correctness warning, not merely a record. EXECUTED, NOT ONLY ASSERTED ABOUT (#2418): src/lib/__tests__/email-message-annotation-strip.test.ts runs this statement against a real PostgreSQL in a disposable per-test schema, wired into the migration-drift CI job as "Test email override annotation strip against PostgreSQL". The text-only pinning it replaces was insufficient by mutation - changing ") AS found ON TRUE" to ") AS found ON TRUE WHERE FALSE" wrote ZERO audit rows while every toContain assertion stayed green. No enum change, no DROP TABLE/COLUMN/TYPE/CONSTRAINT, no RENAME, no ALTER COLUMN TYPE/SET NOT NULL, and no Xero/Stripe/SES/AI provider call runs in-migration. Old-code compatible in both directions: a draining previous colour reading a stripped override sends the same email minus text it should never have sent, and a new colour reading an un-stripped override behaves exactly as it did before. Re-running selects no rows, changes nothing and writes no second audit entry. Forward-only (no automated rollback): the previous wording of every changed row is in its audit metadata.

Retry-time booking-email authority context (#2362). Additive EXPAND only: ALTER TABLE "EmailLog" adds nullable TEXT "bookingRecipientMemberId" and "bookingRetryHtmlBody" plus nullable BOOLEAN "bookingBodyOverrideApplied" and "bookingDetailLinkIncluded", all with NO default, NO backfill, NO index and NO foreign key. PostgreSQL adds all four columns as metadata-only catalog changes with no table rewrite or row scan; the one statement takes a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on EmailLog for the catalog write. EmailLog is high-volume but absent from HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX, so the blue/green validator is silent by design; this voluntary row records the lock and compatibility argument. Old-colour compatible forward: the deployed client never selects or writes these columns, so old-colour rows leave all four NULL. New-colour retry treats an old-colour booking row's NULL provenance as unknown legacy context, retires it at MAX attempts, drops the retained body and requires a reviewed manual re-send instead of inferring authority from the recipient address. New-colour sends write the checked member id (or NULL for public/aggregate mail), override/link provenance, and put retryable booking HTML ONLY in bookingRetryHtmlBody while leaving legacy htmlBody NULL; sensitive/non-retryable templates remain NULL in both. This is the reverse/rollback safety mechanism, not a timing assumption: the pre-#2362 worker's executable query requires htmlBody IS NOT NULL, so after a rollback it cannot select or resend a new-version FAILED booking row containing retained authenticated HTML. The current worker selects either storage shape, rechecks booking authority plus current direct/inherited mailbox ownership, and atomically guards on both body columns before sending. The included-link bit also fails closed if application-origin drift means a known retained href cannot be safely located. Existing rows remain EmailLog audit records; no row is deleted or backfilled, and their subject/status/error history remains. No enum change, DROP, RENAME, SET NOT NULL, type conversion, DML, session-clock write, provider call, transaction participant, advisory-lock key or long-running index/constraint validation exists. Forward-only expand: the columns remain safely through application rollback, and rollback intentionally pauses automatic retry of new-version booking rows until the authority-aware worker is restored. Run in the normal deploy window and let the deploy lock timeout stop the brief catalog lock if EmailLog is unexpectedly busy.

Index MemberSubscription.xeroInvoiceId so "who else does this Xero invoice cover?" stops sequentially scanning the table (#2400 review, F8). Additive EXPAND only, ONE statement: CREATE INDEX "MemberSubscription_xeroInvoiceId_idx" ON "MemberSubscription"("xeroInvoiceId"). It is here because CREATE INDEX against "MemberSubscription" trips HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX in scripts/validate-blue-green-migrations.sh; nothing in the file matches BREAKING_SQL_REGEX or DESTRUCTIVE_REMOVAL_SQL_REGEX. Why the index: #2400 made both the admin cancellation review queue and every approval ask which members a subscription invoice still covers, which reads MemberSubscription with where xeroInvoiceId IN (...). The column carried no index at all, so each of those reads was a full sequential scan; the queue page asked it once per page load and the approval guard once per approval. The PR also threads a single credit-plan map through the queue's two consumers so the read happens once per page rather than twice, but the scan itself is what this index removes. LOCK IMPACT: a plain (non-CONCURRENT) CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on MemberSubscription for the length of the build. SHARE permits concurrent reads but BLOCKS writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) on that table until it commits, and because Prisma wraps the whole migration file in one transaction the lock is held to COMMIT rather than released statement by statement. The writers that would wait are the membership subscription billing confirm/reconcile paths, the Xero subscription-invoice create/void sync, manual mark-paid, and the season roll-forward — none of which is on a member-facing hot path, and all of which are idempotent and retried. The build itself is a single btree over one nullable TEXT column on a club-scale table (one row per member per season: low thousands of rows for a club of a few hundred members after a decade), so the window is milliseconds to low seconds. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY is deliberately NOT used and is not available: PostgreSQL forbids it inside a transaction block and Prisma always wraps a migration in one, exactly as recorded for 20260731120100_add_booking_guest_consent. If MemberSubscription ever grew past what a SHARE-locked build can take in a deploy window, the index would have to be built out of band, not by editing this migration. The deploy guard's lock timeout is the backstop. No enum change, no DROP TABLE/COLUMN/TYPE/CONSTRAINT, no RENAME, no ALTER COLUMN TYPE/SET NOT NULL, no ADD CONSTRAINT and so no FK validation and no lock on "Member", no backfill DML, no session-clock write, and no Xero/Stripe/SES/provider call runs in-migration. Old-colour compatible in BOTH directions, trivially so: an index is invisible to the Prisma client. The previously deployed colour issues exactly the same SQL it issued before and gets exactly the same rows back, only faster where the planner picks the new index; no column, type, constraint or default is added, changed or removed, so no row's shape or value differs by one byte and nothing can fail to deserialise. The reverse direction is equally safe: anything the NEW colour writes to MemberSubscription during the migrate->cutover drain is an ordinary row in the pre-existing shape. Rollback is a DROP INDEX that loses nothing but the speed-up. Timestamp coordination: 20260801160000 sorts strictly after every committed migration, the latest being 20260801150000_strip_email_override_bracket_annotations, and reuses no existing prefix (it was renamed from 20260801120000 and again from 20260801150000 as each prefix was claimed by a migration merged to main first) (the duplicate-prefix ratchet in scripts/check-migration-safety-coverage.sh turns main red on a collision). FOREIGN KEY takes SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on Member plus a row-share lock on the referenced table, which is the same table; both are brief at this row count. Statement 1 records who was chosen behind each existing pointer, re-seating a TRANSITIVE pointer (one naming somebody who is not a direct parent, only reachable under the retired multi-hop walk) onto a direct parent. Statement 2 derives the effective pointer from that choice: it is kept only while the chosen member is an adult, not archived, holds a real rather than club-internal .invalid address, and does not themselves inherit. THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO PARENTAGE TEST in this statement, and the distinction matters to anyone reading the post-deploy list: a hand-picked source naming an unrelated adult, and a family-group login cluster pointed at its holder, are both legitimate and both survive. One hop is enforced where a CHOICE is RECORDED (statement 1's ancestry test, and the application's writers), never on the keep condition here. An operator expecting this migration to drop every pointer whose target is not a parent will read the resulting list as too short and wrongly conclude it under-ran. What it observes is a VALUE change on that column for exactly the transitive pointers this issue exists to correct: notifications for those members move from a grandparent to the direct parent, or stop resolving to anybody, which is the decided behaviour and not a fault of the drain. The one thing a draining old colour can still do is write a fresh transitive pointer; the new colour converges it, because reconciliation is a total, idempotent function of the tree that the daily email-inheritance-reconcile cron re-runs over every member. Repeating the whole migration is not itself idempotent and is not claimed to be — but the reason is the DDL, not the DML: the file opens with ADD COLUMN without IF NOT EXISTS, so a re-run fails 42701 before any data statement is reached. The DML itself is convergent, and an earlier version of this row claimed otherwise (that statement 1 would re-seat a choice statement 2 had cleared, which cannot happen: no statement in this migration ever clears a choice, and statement 1's WHERE excludes rows whose pointer was nulled). That mattered because an operator recovering from a partial apply would have hand-repaired rows the file would have converged. The application-level sweep is the re-runnable half and is what recovery uses. Repairs the dates of birth the two defective Xero parsers stored a day early (#2859). PURE VALUE REPAIR, NO SCHEMA CHANGE: one UPDATE on "Member"."dateOfBirth" and nothing else. THIS ROW IS REQUIRED, not documentation: "Member" IS in HOT_TABLE_SQL_REGEX and the statement is an UPDATE on it. WHAT IT MATCHES: a stored dateOfBirth whose time-of-day is exactly 11:00:00.000, 12:00:00.000 or 13:00:00.000 UTC (New Zealand local midnight at +13 and +12, plus 13 as a known-inert safety margin), moved forward onto UTC midnight of the intended day by date_trunc('day', dateOfBirth + INTERVAL '13 hours'). Minute and second must both be exactly zero, because the claim being made about a matched row is that it is EXACTLY a local midnight. EXPECT TEN ROWS CHANGED, NOT 364: the measured population is 10 of the 375 members who hold a date of birth (six at 11:00, four at 12:00) on the one deployment with a Xero connection. An earlier census reported 364 of 375 and is RETRACTED - it applied AT TIME ZONE to this naive column and read it back through the session zone, which inverted the result. Ten is the number to expect; a run that reports 364 means something is wrong, not that it went well. Every other deployment picks up the corrected parser before it ever imports a contact and this statement matches nothing there - because they never ran the defective parser, NOT because the predicate is zone-neutral (reading hours 11-13 as local midnight of the NEXT day is sound only for a server 11-13h EAST of UTC; the Dockerfile pins TZ=Pacific/Auckland). LOCK IMPACT: a single UPDATE taking ROW EXCLUSIVE on "Member" alone. There is no index on dateOfBirth, so it is a sequential scan of a table in the low thousands of rows - sub-second - and it writes only the matched rows. No foreign key is touched, no trigger fans out, no other table is referenced, and no Booking, Payment, capacity or provider record is read or written. It blocks a concurrent Member writer for that instant only. Run in the normal deploy window and let the deploy guard stop on lock timeout. NO SESSION CLOCK: no CURRENT_TIMESTAMP or now() anywhere, so the #1627 session-clock DML gate is satisfied; the arithmetic is a constant INTERVAL against the stored value. updatedAt is DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED (raw SQL bypasses Prisma's @updatedAt): moving it would make every repaired member look as though somebody had just edited their record, and the verification fixture asserts every non-dateOfBirth column is byte-identical. OLD-CODE COMPATIBLE, and strictly IMPROVED rather than merely tolerated. The column's type, nullability and name are unchanged, so a draining old colour neither gains nor loses a field and its writers are unaffected. What changes for it is the VALUE, and every old-colour reader gets a better answer: the UTC readers (member CSV export, the member's own data export, the admin member-detail edit form, the family card - all toISOString().slice(0,10) shaped) render the PREVIOUS day for a defective row today and render the correct day after the repair; the club-zone and local-getter readers (computeAge in policies/age-tier.ts, member-age.ts) already recovered the intended day from the defective instant under the TZ=Pacific/Auckland pin and read that same day afterwards, so nothing they decide moves. No age tier changes in either colour, which is the property that keeps pricing and hosting eligibility still - argued at code level rather than measured, and CONFIRM IT with the age-tier reconciliation query in the pull request's manual checks after the run (an empty result is the proof). TWO BOUNDED DRAIN INTERACTIONS. First, the old colour still carries the defective parser, so a Xero contact import run on it after this migration writes a fresh local-midnight row. THE REMEDY IS NOT "re-run the migration": prisma migrate deploy has already recorded this migration as applied and will never run it again. The operator must execute the statement BY HAND against the database after the drain, and it is reproduced here so they do not have to reconstruct it: UPDATE "Member" SET "dateOfBirth" = date_trunc('day', "dateOfBirth" + INTERVAL '13 hours') WHERE "dateOfBirth" IS NOT NULL AND date_part('hour', "dateOfBirth") IN (11, 12, 13) AND date_part('minute', "dateOfBirth") = 0 AND date_part('second', "dateOfBirth") = 0; It is idempotent and value-scoped, so running it a second time on already-repaired data changes nothing. Second, the old colour's age-up cron still compares a stored instant against a local-midnight cutoff, so during the drain it can skip a member whose birthday is exactly the season-start anniversary; the new colour's widened prefilter catches them on its next run. REVERSE ROLLBACK: there is no down migration and none is wanted - rolling the code back does not un-repair the data, and should not, because the repaired value is the correct calendar day under old and new code alike. IDEMPOTENT AND SAFE TO REPLAY: a row at 00:00 can never match the predicate again, so re-running the statement after cutover cannot walk a date of birth forward a second day. EXPECT THE NZBN FIELD TO FILL IN GRADUALLY, NOT AT DEPLOY (owner decision, 15 Aug 2026). This release starts SENDING each member date of birth to their Xero contact NZBN field, but only when that contact is next created or updated - i.e. when something on the member record actually changes. There is NO backfill and NO bulk push, deliberately: pushing 375 dates of birth into the club accounting system in one unattended write was judged the larger risk, so the owner chose to let it fill in naturally. CONSEQUENCE THE OPERATOR WILL BE ASKED ABOUT: on the day this deploys, and for some time after, most members Xero contacts will still show an EMPTY NZBN field. That is expected and is not a failure of this release. It is also not something to fix with a sweep. THE ACTIONABLE ANSWER when somebody asks why one member NZBN is still blank: touch any mapped field on that member (email, phone, either address, or the date of birth itself) and save. That queues a contact update, which carries the date of birth, and the field populates immediately. Note the write is also skipped, by design, for any contact this app has never observed and did not create - see INV-INT-017 - so a contact that was matched to a member rather than created by the app fills in only once a contact sync has cached it. ORDERING - RUN THE WITNESS QUERY BEFORE THE FIRST POST-DEPLOY CONTACT SYNC. Three further rows sit at 00:00 and are exactly one day behind their Xero contact (an administrator re-saving an affected record before the fix), and they are identifiable ONLY by comparing the stored value against the contact's own companyNumber string. This release makes the app WRITE the app's value over Xero's on the next contact update, so once a sync has run that evidence is gone. Take the three-row list, and the 79-row no-witness list, before any contact sync runs on the new colour. Both queries are in the pull request's manual checks.
